headline: KSE-100 grinds 0.23% higher to 175,329 as hot US jobs data revives Fed hike bets and Brent nears $97 on Iran-Kuwait strikes
mood: Hawkish Fed repricing, Hormuz risk climbing · KSE-100 holds firm

snapshot.label: US 10Y / 2Y
snapshot.delta: hot jobs data · hike bets firm

five_things.html: An outsized August payrolls beat — +162,000 jobs against a 53,000 consensus, with unemployment steady at 4.1% — pushed the 10-year Treasury yield to 4.78% and the 2-year to 4.34%, its highest since January 2025, as traders lifted the odds of a hike at the 15–16 September FOMC to near 60% on CME FedWatch. Fed Governor Waller had argued the committee could “wait one meeting” for disinflation to show, but the data cuts against that case. Sources: CNBC, USAGOLD.

The S&P 500 fell 0.38% to 7,718.60, the Dow lost 0.51% to 53,414.25 and the Nasdaq eased 0.29% to 26,506.99 on Friday as the hot jobs print reversed the week's rate-cut optimism and pulled equities off their highs. Sources: Washington Post, TheStreet.

Crude extended its advance toward three-month highs on Monday — Brent at $97.47/bbl (+1.24%) and WTI at $92.59/bbl (+1.22%) — after Iranian strikes hit US-linked bases in Kuwait on 2–3 September, keeping a Strait of Hormuz risk premium bid even as OPEC+'s seven core members head into their 6 September meeting expected to hold quotas steady into Q4. Sources: Trading Economics, Rio Times.

five_things.chip: KSE-100 Grinds to a Firmer Close
five_things.html: The benchmark added 399.14 points (0.23%) to close at 175,328.82 on Friday, swinging between an intraday low of 174,515.38 and a high of 175,418.29. Ready-market volume rose to 874.32 million shares worth Rs32.42bn, with breadth split 235 advancers to 218 decliners (43 unchanged). MEBL, BAHL, MARI, PPL and OGDC added a combined 250 points; UBL, ATRL, PSEL, Cnergyico and FFC dragged the index down 212 points as rising oil prices kept investors cautious. Sources: Business Recorder.

five_things.chip: Pakistan CPI Back in Double Digits
five_things.html: August CPI accelerated to 11.1% y/y from 9.2% in July — urban inflation at 10.4%, rural at 12.2% — on higher food and fuel costs, complicating the SBP's path after it held its policy rate at 11.5% for a second straight meeting in July. KIBOR has begun inching up in sympathy, with 6-month paper at 11.61–11.86% as of Friday. Sources: Business Recorder, PBS.

matrix.local_html: Pakistan's macro picture turned more complicated this week: August CPI jumped to 11.1% y/y from 9.2% in July, its first double-digit print in months, even as the KSE-100 added 0.23% to close at 175,328.82 on Friday on broad-based buying in banks, autos and E&P. SBP foreign reserves rose to $17.12bn in the week to 28 August, with FY26 remittances tracking toward $42bn, and the central bank holds its policy rate at 11.5% into a September MPC that now looks more finely balanced given the inflation resurgence and a firmer oil import bill. USD/PKR interbank held little changed near 277.50. Sources: Business Recorder, ProPakistani.
matrix.gcc_html: Gulf non-oil momentum stayed resilient despite the conflict backdrop: the UAE's S&P Global PMI rose to 55.3 in August from 52.7, its fastest pace since December 2024, while Saudi Arabia's Riyad Bank PMI climbed to a six-month high of 53.8. That strength is being tested by a firmer oil tape — Brent near $97.5/bbl on renewed Iran-Kuwait strikes — as OPEC+'s seven core members head into a 6 September meeting expected to hold quotas steady into Q4 after completing their planned 2026 output-cut unwind. Saudi's PIF, meanwhile, is executing its board-approved 2026–2030 strategy prioritising tourism, travel and domestic ecosystem investment as Vision 2030 enters its final stretch. Sources: The National, Arab News.
matrix.global_html: A blowout August payrolls report reset the rate-cut narrative: nonfarm payrolls added 162,000 versus 53,000 expected, unemployment held at 4.1%, and Treasury yields jumped — the 10-year to 4.78%, the 2-year to 4.34% — lifting the odds of a hike at the 15–16 September FOMC meeting toward 60% even as Fed Governor Waller argues for patience. Equities retreated in response (S&P 500 −0.38%) while gold slid 1.3% to $4,420/oz on a firmer dollar. The other swing factor is the Middle East: continued US-Iran strikes, including missiles on Kuwait, have pushed Brent within reach of $100/bbl for the first time since Q2. Sources: CNBC, Trading Economics.

legislative.policy_html: FBR SRO 1495(I)/2026 amends the Tax Year 2026 income tax return form just weeks ahead of the 30 September filing deadline, adding new schedule provisions.
legislative.sectors: Salaried & corporate taxpayers, tax practitioners, compliance software
legislative.impact_html: Wins: Tax advisory and compliance-software firms billing for last-minute adjustments; FBR gains finer-grained disclosure ahead of its Rs15.3tn FY27 collection target. Loses: Individual and corporate filers facing compressed timelines, with practitioners flagging legal uncertainty over the notification's timing.

legislative.policy_html: OPEC+'s seven core members head into their 6 September meeting expected to hold quotas steady into Q4 after completing the 188,000 bpd September output increase.
legislative.sectors: Oil & gas majors, Gulf shipping/insurance, non-oil private sector
legislative.impact_html: Wins: Saudi Arabia (PMI 53.8) and UAE (PMI 55.3) non-oil sectors, which extend multi-month growth highs on quota discipline and steady supply. Loses: Gulf shippers, insurers and energy importers exposed to a rising Hormuz risk premium as Brent approaches $100/bbl.

legislative.policy_html: The Fed's 15–16 September FOMC meeting looms with hike odds near 60% on CME FedWatch after a hot August jobs report, even as Governor Waller pushes back on tightening this cycle.
legislative.sectors: Rate-sensitive equities, EM currencies (incl. PKR), energy majors
legislative.impact_html: Wins: The dollar and short-end yields, which firmed on hike repricing; energy majors benefiting from a rising Brent/WTI complex. Loses: Rate-sensitive equities and EM currencies, including the PKR, which face tighter-for-longer risk if the Fed does hike in September.

levels.support_note: Friday's intraday low (174,515); deeper support at 173,500

desk_stance_html: Friday's 0.23% gain masks a genuinely two-sided tape: banks, autos and E&P names such as MEBL, MARI, PPL and OGDC did the heavy lifting as the oil rally lifted energy earnings expectations, while UBL, Cnergyico and FFC dragged, and volume rose alongside the index — a mild positive for conviction. The bigger risk sits offshore: a hawkish US jobs surprise has revived Fed hike odds into the 15–16 September FOMC, and Brent's push toward $100/bbl on renewed Iran-Kuwait strikes worsens Pakistan's import bill just as August CPI printed back in double digits at 11.1%. We'd stay selectively long E&P and banks as oil-rally beneficiaries while trimming broader beta into the SBP's September MPC and any fresh Hormuz escalation. All levels are indicative desk estimates, not recommendations.

KSE-100 grinds 0.23% higher to 175,329 as hot US jobs data revives Fed hike bets and Brent nears $97 on Iran-Kuwait strikes

Good morning — here's the ContexAi Research desk's read on markets for Monday, 07 September 2026, covering Friday's close.

THE OVERNIGHT TAPE
The S&P 500 fell 0.38% to 7,718.60, the Dow lost 0.51% to 53,414.25 and the Nasdaq eased 0.29% to 26,506.99 on Friday after a blowout August payrolls report — +162,000 jobs versus 53,000 expected, unemployment steady at 4.1% — pushed the 10-year Treasury yield to 4.78% and the 2-year to 4.34%, lifting the odds of a hike at the 15–16 September FOMC to near 60% on CME FedWatch, even as Fed Governor Waller argues the committee can "wait one meeting" for disinflation. Gold slid 1.3% to $4,420/oz and silver eased to $66.30 as the dollar firmed. Brent pushed toward $97.5/bbl and WTI near $92.6/bbl on renewed Iran-Kuwait strikes, approaching three-month highs.

PAKISTAN
The KSE-100 added 399.14 points (0.23%) to close at 175,328.82 on Friday, swinging between 174,515 and 175,418 intraday. Ready-market volume rose to 874.32 million shares worth Rs32.42bn, with breadth split 235 advancers to 218 decliners. MEBL, BAHL, MARI, PPL and OGDC led gainers while UBL, ATRL, PSEL, Cnergyico and FFC lagged as rising oil prices kept investors cautious. August CPI accelerated to 11.1% y/y from 9.2% in July, complicating the SBP's path after it held its policy rate at 11.5% in July. SBP reserves rose to $17.12bn and USD/PKR interbank held near 277.50.

GCC
The UAE's non-oil PMI rose to 55.3 in August, its fastest pace since December 2024, while Saudi Arabia's PMI climbed to a six-month high of 53.8, both showing resilience despite the conflict backdrop. OPEC+'s seven core members head into a 6 September meeting expected to hold quotas steady into Q4. Saudi's PIF continues executing its board-approved 2026–2030 strategy prioritising tourism, travel and domestic investment under Vision 2030.

GLOBAL
The hot US jobs report reset the rate-cut narrative just as it looked like the Fed had room to ease, sending yields and the dollar higher and pressuring both equities and gold. The other swing factor remains the Middle East, where continued US-Iran strikes, including missiles on Kuwait, have pushed Brent within reach of $100/bbl for the first time since Q2.

LEGISLATIVE TRACKER
• Pakistan: FBR SRO 1495(I)/2026 amends the 2026 tax return form weeks ahead of the 30 September filing deadline.
• GCC: OPEC+ heads into its 6 September meeting expected to hold quotas steady into Q4.
• Global: The Fed's 15–16 September FOMC meeting looms with hike odds near 60% after the jobs shock.

THE DAY AHEAD
KSE-100 — Support 174,500 (deeper support 173,500) · Pivot 175,329 (Friday's close) · Resistance 175,400 (Friday's intraday high, then 176,000).

Desk stance: Friday's gain masks a two-sided tape — E&P and banks did the heavy lifting on the oil rally while broader breadth stayed thin. The bigger risk sits offshore: revived Fed hike odds and Brent's push toward $100/bbl worsen Pakistan's import bill just as CPI printed back in double digits. We favour a selective tilt toward E&P and banks while trimming broader beta into the SBP's September MPC and any fresh Hormuz escalation. All levels are indicative desk estimates, not recommendations.
